distinguishing_features: A continuous-flow WHIMS permanent-magnet channel with a wall-gradient field, absent from the batch dosing/recirculation prior art.
Separation based on diamagnetic susceptibility differences and lateral magnetophoretic drift of dissolved Li, Mg, and B species rather than conductivity-gated chemical dosing.
A wall ion-selective membrane/electrokinetic coupling element added to the magnetic separator, whereas the prior art installs no new hardware.
An outlet impurity-removal test using ICP-MS/AAS and a 15% Mg/B reduction threshold within one residence time.
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to selectively reduce dissolved boron and magnesium impurity concentrations in a lithium brine stream during continuous operation to obtain battery-grade product purity.
parsed.viable_reason: The stated magnetophoretic drift is about 4e-14 m/s at the upper assumed susceptibility difference and gradient, giving sub-nanometre displacement in 1-5 s and being dwarfed by diffusion, so it cannot remove Mg/B across a 10 mm channel.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Prior art 1 relies on conductivity-gated dosing and recirculation to reduce scaling potential and provides no teaching or motivation to use ionic diamagnetic susceptibility differences in a WHIMS channel, so the feature is not a routine parameter change.
